items.note: Press release dated 15 April 2025 (Métropole, Ville de Lyon, SYTRAL Mobilités) states ZTL and new traffic plan from 21 June 2025; permanent and occasional ayants-droit; 6h-13h bornes basses / 13h-6h bornes hautes; perimeter guarantees access to the 18 car parks of the Presqu'île and surroundings, nearly 10,000 spaces. Date 2025-06-21 is the stated start date (announcement was 15 April). Title matches.

Leaflet lists Crit'Air 5/unclassified banned since 1 Jan 2023, Crit'Air 4 since 1 Jan 2024, Crit'Air 3 since 1 Jan 2025 for cars and motorised two-wheelers; defines the ZFE as restricting both circulation and parking. 'ZFE PART web FEVRIER25' is only the file name; the PDF title/cover is 'ZFE, la Métropole vous accompagne' (Zone à Faibles Émissions).
items.corrected_title: Zone à Faibles Émissions : la Métropole vous accompagne

items.note: LyonMag 30 Jan 2024: Ville de Lyon presented weight-based grids (thresholds differ for thermal, plug-in hybrid and electric), resident monthly rate from 20 euros to 15/30/45; to be voted at the March council and implemented in June. Correctly framed as a plan subject to a vote. Title and date match.

Figures are on the page (-~20% hourly use in wider Presqu'île car parks in just over two years; decline steeper from Sept 2024 roadworks and then the ZTL; +31% hourly since 2019, +26% resident, +30% unlimited subscriptions). But the page ties 'since 2019' only to the hourly rate, and 'over the same period' wrongly merges the two-year usage window with the since-2019 price window. Date: PDF header reads 'Lyon, le 9 avril 2026', but the file name, PDF creation metadata (2026-06-09), the text ('accessible à partir du 9 juin') and Lyon Capitale ('Le 9 juin, l'exécutif avait présenté son plan d'actions') all support 9 June 2026, so the date is kept. Title matches.
items.corrected_text: The Métropole said hourly use of car parks in the wider Presqu'île fell by nearly 20% in just over two years, with the decline steepening from September 2024 during major roadworks and again after the ZTL was introduced. It also said tariffs had risen sharply: 31% for hourly parking since 2019, 26% for resident subscriptions and 30% for unlimited subscriptions.

items.note: Same release: February 2026 results of the Presqu'île monitoring surveys; among residents who noticed changes in the last six months, 67% saw a negative impact and 26% say they come to the Presqu'île less often.

LPA release dated 31 July 2026: from 1 Aug 2026 tariffs frozen (hourly and subscriptions) in line with Métropole orientations, at Bourse, Hôtel de Ville, République, Perrache, Terreaux, Célestins, Antonin Poncet, Cordeliers, Saint-Antoine, Grolée plus Saint-Jean, Saint-Georges, Morand (13). Title matches.
Lyon Capitale 2 July 2026: a 6%-a-year rise in LPA car-park tariffs, voted to 2032 by the former majority and scheduled for 1 August, has been frozen. Title and date match.

Same article: the Métropole 'souhaite instaurer' a weekday ZTL (Mon-Thu 19h-5h) and a weekend ZTL (Fri 15h to Mon 5h) - a proposal, correctly framed. Rue Grenette reopening 'vraisemblablement à la rentrée de septembre' with 'plusieurs scénarios à l'étude'.

LyonMag 5 June 2026: Emmanuel Hamelin, Métropole vice-president and former deputy, elected president of the SEM Lyon Parc Auto for six years, made official 'this week'; this supports June 2026 as the date. The article body does not name his predecessor; Fabien Bagnon appears only in reader comments, so 'succeeding Fabien Bagnon' must go.
items.corrected_text: Emmanuel Hamelin, a vice-president of the Métropole, was elected president of the mixed-economy company (SEM) Lyon Parc Auto for a six-year term.

items.note: The cited LPA release (31 July 2026) supports the DSP operator role, 38 car parks, 22 P+R, nearly 400 EV charge points, 50,000 on-street spaces, 6,700 secure bike spaces, 270 staff and 86.2 MEUR revenue in 2025. The 'four entities (SEM, SPL, GE, GIE)' description from August 2025 is in the Terreaux release, not this source, so it is dropped.
items.corrected_text: LPA Mobilités operates car parks for the Métropole under public-service delegation contracts. It reported 38 car parks, 22 park-and-ride sites, nearly 400 EV charge points, 50,000 on-street spaces, 6,700 secure bike spaces, 270 staff and 86.2 million euros of revenue in 2025.

items.note: LPA release dated 29 Aug 2025: reopening 2 Sept 2025 after four months of works; 4.5 MEUR fully funded by the Métropole; Smart Parking Ticketless with Hitachi Rail, plate reading, 'une première à Lyon dans un parc de stationnement public', progressively activated; per-space guidance; 40 EV charge points (14 at 22 kW); 537 bike spaces. Only levels -1 and -4 reopened on 2 Sept (others in October), which the text does not contradict. Title matches.

LyonMag 2 Feb 2022 supports the 122 MEUR investment over six years for diversification, doubling EV charge points from 160 to 300 by end 2022, more bike parking and car-sharing. The 354 (Aug 2025) and nearly 400 (July 2026) counts are not on this page and are dropped.
items.corrected_text: LPA announced a six-year, 122-million-euro investment plan to diversify beyond parking, including doubling its EV charge points from 160 to 300 by the end of 2022 and expanding bike parking and car-sharing.

items.note: Indigo release dated 2/12/2024: single-level Bellecour car park inaugurated 1967, extended this year on the remains of a former service station; closed Cyclopark for 100 bikes and three new EV charge points. Title matches.

ONLYLYON 'Chiffres clés du tourisme 2024': 9.56 million commercial overnight stays, annual hotel occupancy (TO) 71.1%, and 2024 figures 'confirment un retour aux standards d'avant 2020'. Title matches.
URL redirects to Lyon Capitale 15 Sept 2025 article with this title; it states more than 519 million trips on TCL in 2024, a ridership record.

corrected_summary: A limited-traffic zone and new traffic plan were set to take effect in Lyon's Presqu'île from 21 June 2025, and the Métropole's low-emission zone has barred Crit'Air 3 cars since 1 January 2025. In June 2026 the Métropole reported that hourly use of Presqu'île car parks had fallen by nearly 20% in just over two years while hourly tariffs had risen 31% since 2019, and LPA Mobilités froze prices at 13 central car parks from 1 August 2026. LPA has also added EV charge points, bike parking and, at Terreaux, ticketless entry by number-plate recognition.
